about: How the kernel reads a model reply: extract_call, then normalize_arguments, exactly as TaskLoop::OnProposed does. Checked by the kernel's Rust tests (tests.rs) and by the benchmark through zephyrus_policy_probe (test_extraction.py), so the browser and the benchmark cannot read a reply differently. `expect` null means no call is read. Most cases are verbatim model output with a recorded failure behind them; add one whenever a reply is misread.

cases.why: The plain form.
Wrapped in prose.
A fence is what the model meant, even when the prose names another tool.

cases.why: `tool` and `parameters` are accepted as well as `name` and `arguments`.
No arguments field means none.
An object with no name is not a call; the scan moves on to the next one.
qwen2.5:7b, verbatim. A bare answer goes into task.complete's one argument. The Python port graded this as a schema failure; the browser runs it.
qwen2.5:1.5b, verbatim. A bare value for a one-argument tool.
Positional arguments inside the JSON form map onto the schema's properties in order.
An argument the tool does not have is dropped, not fatal.
The same in the call form: `filter` is not a page.find argument.
Null arguments are kept as they are, so validation names the problem.
An unknown tool is still read; the contract check refuses it by name.
qwen2.5:7b wrote calls, not JSON, twenty times out of twenty in one traced run.
